title: Do we need the base classes?
body:
I want to raise this issue, not because I think we can action on it soon, but because I want people to know it's definitely on our minds. It's more that we want to keep in mind this possibility as we make higher-level decisions.

If we kill high-water marks somehow (#13, or #24), then most of the value-add of `WritableStream` over `BaseWritableStream` and `ReadableStream` over `BaseReadableStream` is gone.

Alternately, if we still want the buffering strategies idea, then maybe it's foolishness to try to have `BaseReadableStream` and `BaseWritableStream` even exist at all. After all, they are just special cases of `ReadableStream` and `WritableStream`, but with very specific buffering strategies. We could just give RS and WS default values for their `strategy` parameter and be done with it.

The only other thing we're adding besides buffering strategies is adding multi-pipe when going from `BaseReadableStream` to `ReadableStream`. That's not a great reason for an inheritance hierarchy though, even if some people keep urging me to layer on top of a simple primitive and keep complicated things like multi-pipe at a higher level. We could either roll it into the single `ReadableStream` class, or we could make people manually create `TeeStream`s, or we could even keep things uber-basic and not support multi-pipe out of the box, but make people write their own `TeeStream`s.

That kind of ties into a larger discussion about what helpers we provide in the base streams library... Ideally I'd like to supply no helpers and then harvest the very best ones from the community after 6 months of these things living in browsers. But then again, I am sympathetic to the argument that provided unusably-low-level APIs is not a good way to kickstart an ecosystem.
